newsitem.title: FRANCE: France reaffirms hope for stability in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France reaffirms hope for stability in Zaire.

text.p: France reaffirmed on Friday its desire for peace and stability in Zaire but declined immediate comment on ailing head of state Mobutu Sese Seko's decision to bow out of power while retaining the title of president.

"France has since the beginning of the crisis called for a peaceful solution," French Defence Minister Charles Millon said. "It wants a guarantee of Zaire's territorial integrity and the re-establishment of civil peace".
"Due to its size and prominence in Africa, stability in Zaire is crucial for stability in the entire region," Millon said in an interview on France 3 television.
Asked how a shift in power to rebel leader Laurent Kabila from Mobutu would affect France, a former colonial power in Africa, Millon responded:
"The problem is not to choose. The problem is to hope that, with democratic elections, a stable regime can be put in place which can help bring about growth in Zaire," he said.
Foreign Ministry officials also had no comment on Mobutu's decision to step aside.

Asked if Mobutu was expected to come to France where he owns a palatial residence on the Riviera, his home during much in recent months, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said: "We have no information on Mr Mobutu's intentions."

Asked if Paris would allow Mobutu entry if he sought refuge here, the spokesman said: "This question cannot be addressed since it is entirely theoretical and based on whether he would want to come. In any case, he has other homes elsewhere."

Analysts said they presumed the French government would not be eager to have Mobutu come to France until after a May 25-June 1 parliamentary election for fear his presence might become an campaign issue.
